chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Usman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the one who makes up for the month of Ramadan in a discontinuous manner. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he has memorized his (number of missed) days, then there is no problem.'

key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to make up missed Ramadan fasts non-consecutively?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Samaanah ibn Mihar reports that Imam al-Sadiq permitted making up missed Ramadan fasts even if they were not observed consecutively, provided the individual retained knowledge of the exact number of days missed. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the intention (*niyyah*) and personal accountability for the count of fasts, offering flexibility for those unable to fast continuously due to work or other obligations. It underscores the principle that the validity of *Qada* (makeup) fasts relies on fulfilling the obligatory count rather than strict chronological continuity.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the one who makes up for a Month of Ramazan with breaks (discontinues manner). He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he has memorised his (number of missed) days, so there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah, who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who fasts Qada’ (compensatory fast) for the fast of the month of Ramadan in separate times. He (the Imam) said, Tt is not harmful if he keeps the number of days without missing.’”
